payload.body: F10 and F15 are covered in 45edf8f, with both optional gaps; 36 bats tests pass and check all is green. F10: the forged-manifest test forges .tag, .identifier and .team_id in turn. F15: the fake codesign can serve a timestamp-less display from a given display on, here the first after sign()'s own (a count taken from the targets list), so only the signed set's own check can refuse before the upload. Optional: a test pins build.yml's SHA256SUMS.ci in both the sha256sum and gh release create lines, and nopython refuses a #! python line in a .md file, which only the #! rule catches. Your F10 mutants also exposed a weaker test helper: refused() relied on set -e, but a loop calls it left of ||, where bash runs a function with set -e off, so each looped refusal passed whatever it checked. It now returns the failure itself. The archive-names loop had the same hole, and a mutant that keeps only each member's last path component is now caught. Each red check was shown red in a throwaway worktree, with each baseline green: tag, identifier, the pre-upload check, the SHA256SUMS.ci name, the #! rule and the names loop.
